I will do it the way I have done around here for years, with a little adjustment if I see the neighbors using something that works better. My land is 7 mu, not very big, so I count every bag I buy. But I will not cut fertilizer too hard, because if wheat or maize comes out weak, that loss is worse than spending a bit extra on fertilizer. For wheat, I will still use improved seed, because now most people around me use that and it stands better and yields better than the old kind. I will put a solid base dressing before sowing, then topdress nitrogen when the wheat turns green in spring. With well water, I will irrigate about 2 times for wheat, usually once after sowing if the ground is dry and once around jointing or booting. For maize after wheat, I will use hybrid seed, because around here that is what people plant and it gives more grain. I will put fertilizer at planting and then add nitrogen again around the big flare stage. I usually do rotary tillage after harvest because it is faster and cheaper on my size of land. I will spray when needed, not too many times, usually enough to keep aphids, armyworms, rust, or leaf disease from getting ahead of me. If the season is normal and water is there, this is the kind of plan I will follow.
